AWARD/JUDGMENT FACTUAL POSITION & PLEADINGS 1.

The present petition was filed on 03/09/2015 which was PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2024.04.16 14:46:02 +0530 related to a motor vehicular accident dated 28.01.2012 at about 11.00 PM in which one Sh. Netra Pal Singh S/o Sh.Kaha Singh (hereinafter referred to as "deceased") lost his life.

As per this petition, at the relevant time, the deceased Netra Pal was working as a driver on vehicle bearing registration no. HR-55E-3231 ( Tata Truck LPK 2518)
(hereinafter referred to as "Vehicle Involved") under the employment of R-1 on unfortunate said day deceased was robbed and murdered by two persons.
An FIR no. 16/12 PS Timar Pur was registered.

It is further stated that the postmortem was conducted by the Subzi Mandi Mortuary of Bara Hindu Rao, Delhi and concerned police handover the body of deceased/R-1 is stated to be the owner/
employer of the deceased Netra Pal of the vehicle involved. R-2 is stated to be the insurer of the vehicle involved.

ISSUES 4.
Vide order dated 10/05/2022, the following issues were framed by the Ld.
Predecessor of this Tribunal :

-
1.Whether on 28.01.2012 at Wazirabad, Near Crossing (Ring Road), ISBT, Sh. Netra Pal Singh received fatal injuries arising out of use PANKAJ by PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA
Date: 2024.04.16 14:46:06 +0530 of Truck bearing Registration No.HR- 55E- 3231?OPP 2
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. Relief.
EVIDENCE 5.
In support of their contentions, the petitioners examined petitioner no. 1 Sh. Kanha Singh, father of the deceased, as PW-1.
PW-1, vide his affidavit Ex. PW1/A, deposed that he is the father of the deceased who sustained fatal injuries in the accident dated 28.01.2012 as mentioned in Para No. 1 of this award.

5.1
He was cross-examined by Ld. Counsel for R-2/ Insurance Company.
In his cross-examination he deposed that he is a farmer and he was not in the Truck bearing registration number HR- 55E-3231 on 28.01.2012 at 11.00 P.M .
He further deposed that he is not an eye witness to the incident in question.
He denied the suggestion that his son Netrapal was not appointed as a driver in the aforesaid vehicle on 28.01.2012.
He further denied the suggestion that his son Netrapal was robbed and murdered due to personal enmity with some unknown person.
He further denied the suggestion that the murder of his son was not committed inside the abovesaid Truck.
He further denied the suggestion that the aforesaid vehicle was not involved in any manner with the death of his son.
5.2 Petitioner's evidence was closed.
6. R-2 examined its official Smt. Bharati Meena as R2W1 in its defence.
She deposed vide her affidavit Ex.R2W1/A.
She relied upon the insurance policy vide Ex.R2W1/1 (Containing three pages)

She was cross-examined by Ld. Counsel for petitioner.
In her cross- examination she deposed that she has been authorised by the company to appear and depose before the Tribunal.
FINDINGS 7.
Oral submissions have been advanced by Ld. Counsel for the parties.

My findings on the above issues are as under:-
"Whether on 28.01.2012 at Wazirabad, Near Crossing (Ring Road), ISBT, Sh. Netra Pal Singh received fatal injuries arising out of use of Truck bearing Registration No.HR-55E- 3231?OPP"
8.
Since, the present petition was filed U/s 163 A MV Act and same was maintainable, therefore, this Tribunal is not required to return any finding as to the rashness or negligence of R-1.
As of now, this Tribunal is supposed to return a judicial finding as to whether or not the deceased lost his life in an accident arising out of the use of offending vehicle.

9. Since the deceased was a drive in the vehicle involved bearing registration no HR-55E-3231 owned by the R-1, as such it is apparent that his death was committed while he was using the said vehicle.

Therefore, the present petition is being treated u/s 163A of MV Act for the purpose of grant of compensation as per the Second Schedule annexed to M.V. Act, prior to the Motor Vehicles Amendment Act, 2019.

5 PANKAJ by PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA

It is not disputed that the deceased lost his life following a robbery attempt and murder,
therefore, this Tribunal holds that the deceased lost his life on 22.01.2012 on account of use of vehicle involved, which was being driven by deceased at the relevant time.
The issue is decided accordingly.

"Whether the petitioners are entitled to any compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?"
11.

As the fatal accident has arisen out of the use of vehicle involved, accordingly, as per Second Schedule annexed to M.V. Act, prior to the Motor Vehicles Amendment Act, 2019, compensation to the tune of Rs. 5,00,000/- is admissible to the petitioners.

The petitioners are also entitled to be granted a sum of Rs. 20,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs. 20,000/- towards loss of estate in terms of propositions laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Rajwati @ Rajjo & Ors.
Vs. United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Civil Appeal No. 8179/2022 decided on 09/12/2022.
The petitioners are also entitled to be granted a sum of Rs. 44,000/- each towards consortium.

The petitioners are thus awarded a sum of Rs. 1,76,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Seventy Six Thousand only)
on account of the untimely death of the deceased due to a motor vehicular accident dated 28.01.2012.

LIABILITY 14.
As already stated above, R-1 being the owner of the offending vehicle, is liable to pay the awarded amount of compensation to petitioner.
However, since the offending vehicle was insured with R-2 at the time of accident, therefore, R-2/ Insurance Company is liable to indemnify R-1 in respect of above liability.

opennyai_summary.decision:
The issue is decided accordingly.
As the fatal accident has arisen out of the use of vehicle involved, accordingly, as per Second Schedule annexed to M.V. Act, prior to the Motor Vehicles Amendment Act, 2019, compensation to the tune of Rs. 5,00,000/- is admissible to the petitioners.
The petitioners are also entitled to be granted a sum of Rs. 20,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs. 20,000/- towards loss of estate in terms of propositions laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Rajwati @ Rajjo & Ors.
Vs. United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Civil Appeal No. 8179/2022 decided on 09/12/2022.
The petitioners are also entitled to be granted a sum of Rs. 44,000/- each towards consortium.
The petitioners are thus awarded a sum of Rs. 1,76,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Seventy Six Thousand only)
on account of the untimely death of the deceased due to a motor vehicular accident dated 28.01.2012.
The petitioners are thus awarded a sum of Rs.7,16,000/- (Rupees Seven Lakhs Sixteen Thousand only) along with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of filing of petition i.e. 03.09.2015.

payable in equal amounts for a period of 1 to 05 months in succession, as per the scheme formulated by Central Motor Vehicles (fifth Amendment) Rules, 2022 [(Directions at serial no. 35, 36 of Procedure for Investigation of Motor Vehicle Accidents (under Rule 150A)].
13.2 Out of the awarded amount, Petitioner No. 3 is awarded a sum of Rs.7,60,000/- (Rupees Seven Lakhs Sixty Thousand Only) and the said amount is directed to be kept with State Bank of India,
Branch Tis Hazari Courts, New Delhi in MACAD in the form of 38 monthly fixed deposit receipts (FDRs) payable in equal amounts for a period of 1 to 38 months in succession, as per the scheme formulated by Central Motor Vehicles (fifth Amendment) Rules, 2022 [(Directions at serial no. 35,
36 of Procedure for Investigation of Motor Vehicle Accidents (under Rule 150A)].
The remaining amount of Rs.85,358/- (Rupees Eighty Five Thousand Three Hundred Fifty Eight Only) is also directed to be released into her above said account, which can be withdrawn and utilized by the Petitioner No. 3.
13.3 Rs.1,20,765/- be kept in FDRs in the name of Petitioners No. 4 till she attains majority with cumulative interest.

10,000/- each for a period of 1 month to 12 months with cumulative interest in the name of Petitioner No. 4.
